device.name: HECTOR humanoid Gazebo simulation
device.vendor: USC Dynamic Robotics and Control Laboratory

facts.text: hector_control initializes ROS with the node name 'hector_control' and the AnonymousName option, and hard-codes the robot name to 'hector'.
CheatIO::initSend advertises ten unitree_legged_msgs/MotorCmd publishers whose names are '/' + _robot_name + '_gazebo/<joint>_controller/command'.
CheatIO::sendCmd sets every MotorCmd.mode to 0x0A and copies q, dq, tau, Kd and Kp before publishing each of the ten messages.
UnitreeJointController::init subscribes to the relative literal 'command' and publishes unitree_legged_msgs/MotorState on name_space + '/state'.
The joint controller includes unitree_legged_msgs/MotorCmd.h and MotorState.h.
UnitreeJointController::update applies the received q/Kp, dq/Kd and tau when mode is PMSM; while mode is BRAKE it sets zero position stiffness, zero velocity, damping 20 and zero torque.
UnitreeJointController::stopping is an empty function.
main.cpp's ShutDown handler prints 'stop' and sets the global running flag to false.
CheatIO subscribes to the absolute /gazebo/model_states topic with a queue size of 1.
CheatIO.h includes gazebo_msgs/ModelStates.h, the declared message type of /gazebo/model_states.
CheatIO::StateCallback selects the model named '<robot_name>_gazebo' and copies its pose and twist into the controller's cheated high state.
biped.launch starts the ten named joint controllers inside controller_manager with ns='/hector_gazebo'.
biped.launch leaves the unitree_gazebo servo node commented out.

The README tells the operator to launch biped.launch, run 'rosrun hector_control hector_ctrl' and click the simulator's start button, and, when the controller does not start, to terminate it, pause and reset the simulator (ctrl + R) and rerun it.
The shipped xacro sets hip_max 45, hip_min -45, hip_velocity_max 21 and hip_torque_max 33.5.
The shipped xacro sets hip2_max 45, hip2_min -45, hip2_velocity_max 21 and hip2_torque_max 33.5.
The shipped xacro sets thigh_max 100, thigh_min -100, thigh_velocity_max 21 and thigh_torque_max 33.5.
The shipped xacro sets calf_max 100, calf_min -100, calf_velocity_max 14 and calf_torque_max 67.
The shipped xacro sets toe_max 100, toe_min -100, toe_velocity_max 21 and toe_torque_max 33.5.
leg.xacro passes hip_torque_max and hip_velocity_max unchanged to the URDF limit's effort and velocity attributes and converts hip_min and hip_max with PI/180 for its lower and upper attributes.

positionLimits clamps a revolute or prismatic joint's commanded position to the URDF lower and upper limits, velocityLimits its velocity to plus or minus the URDF velocity limit, and effortLimits its torque to plus or minus the URDF effort limit.
runFSMController runs the FSM controller in a loop paced by ros::Rate(1000) while the running flag is true.
biped.launch declares the paused argument with default true and passes it to gazebo_ros's empty_world.launch.
The repository is licensed under the BSD 3-Clause license.
The vendored unitree_legged_control joint controller states that it is Unitree Robotics code governed by the MPL-2.0 license.
gazebo.xacro loads the gazebo_ros_control plugin libgazebo_ros_control.so with robotNamespace /hector_gazebo.
UnitreeJointController::setCommandCB copies mode, q, Kp, dq, Kd and tau of the received MotorCmd into lastCmd and writes it to the realtime command buffer.
joint_controller.h defines PMSM as 0x0A and BRAKE as 0x00.
biped.launch includes gazebo_ros's empty_world.launch.
The gazebo_ros gzserver wrapper adds libgazebo_ros_api_plugin to the server's plugins unless the arguments already name it.
empty_world.launch starts the Gazebo server as the node named gazebo of package gazebo_ros, with the physics engine argument -e $(arg physics).
empty_world.launch defaults its physics argument to ode.
empty_world.launch defaults its gui argument to true.
When gui is true, empty_world.launch starts the node gazebo_gui of type gzclient.
The API plugin calls ros::init with the node name gazebo when ROS is not initialised yet.
The API plugin creates its node handle in the private namespace ~ and advertises its topics and services there.
The API plugin advertises the service pause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on its own callback queue gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service unpause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service get_physics_properties with the gazebo_msgs::GetPhysicsProperties type on gazebo_queue_.
gazeboQueueThread serves gazebo_queue_ in a loop with a 0.001 s wall-clock wait while the node handle is ok.
pausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(true) and returns true.
unpausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(false) and returns true.
getPhysicsProperties sets res.pause to world_->IsPaused().
getPhysicsProperties sets success true only when the physics engine type is ode; for any other engine it sets success false and returns false.
The GetPhysicsProperties response field pause is true if the physics engine is paused.
Among the world-update begin hooks that its comment says apply forces and publish sim time on /clock, the API plugin connects publishSimTime.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.
GazeboRosControlPlugin connects its Update method to the world-update begin event.
GazeboRosControlPlugin::Update reads the simulated robot state, runs the controller manager update and writes the resulting commands to the Gazebo model.
The API plugin advertises the model_states topic (gazebo_msgs::ModelStates) with onModelStatesConnect as its connect callback.
When the first subscriber of the model states connects, the API plugin connects publishModelStates to the world-update begin event.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned ModelStates replies; no physics step, controller loop or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free protocol transport: it answers the /gazebo/model_states subscription, the ten MotorCmd publications and the two companion Gazebo services but runs no Gazebo, joint controllers, contacts, sensors or the hector_control walking loop
the model names, poses and twists are placeholders and the pose nudge after a command is a canned effect, not simulated physics
the package does not bind the per-joint MotorState publishers because the clone composes those names at run time; joint position/velocity feedback is not exposed

the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause: the fake keeps a paused flag that /gazebo/pause_physics sets and /gazebo/get_physics_properties reports, and it does not serve /gazebo/unpause_physics; it runs no Gazebo World::Step or gazebo_ros_control update, and its GetPhysicsProperties numbers are placeholders; the BRAKE mode and the optional unitree_gazebo servo node are not safe-state bindings

while paused, a live Gazebo runs no world update, so gazebo_ros_control applies no torque and /gazebo/model_states and /clock are silent; the fake silences /gazebo/model_states while its flag is set, and the device resource reads no topic (the MotorCmd receipts report the values they sent)
a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI that biped.launch opens by default, by a WorldControl message or by any ROS client; MHS does not watch the flag after the e-stop

the read-back needs the ODE engine (empty_world.launch's default): with another engine get_physics_properties returns false and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held; a graph without gazebo_ros has neither service
the deployment's gazebo_ros and Gazebo must be the pinned 2.9.3 (Noetic) and 11 releases the companion citations name; rosbridge cannot read their versions

no unpause is offered (SAFE-042): the joint controllers keep their stored MotorCmd (joint_controller.cpp:33-45) and apply it in update (139-185); the package cannot clear it first. BRAKE (158-164) sets zero position stiffness, zero velocity, damping 20 and zero torque, so it removes the position stiffness and applies damping only. A PMSM command sets the position target it names (142-145), and the package reads no joint position. starting() (117-129) holds the current position with zero velocity and torque, but gazebo_ros_control calls the controller manager only from its world-update hook (gazebo_ros_control_plugin.cpp:196-199, 251), and World::Step does not run that hook while paused (World.cc:835-854). When hector_ctrl runs, the main loop calls CheatIO::sendRecv (main.cpp:80-83; ros::Rate(1000) at main.cpp:41) and sendCmd publishes all ten MotorCmd messages with mode forced to 0x0A (CheatIO.cpp:34-36, 44-58). The FSM loop (main.cpp:22-30) is a different thread. GazeboRosControlPlugin::Reset (260-266) clears timing, not lastCmd. The constructor zeros lastCmd (joint_controller.cpp:15-18) and biped.launch starts paused (biped.launch:7). ShutDown on SIGINT sets running false (main.cpp:16-20, 78); the README's ctrl+\ (Readme.md:68) is SIGQUIT and is not that handler. After mhs.safety.reset the world stays paused; the operator stops hector_ctrl, relaunches biped.launch and presses the simulator start button outside MHS (Readme.md:61-68)

while hector_ctrl runs (the README's operator step), the main loop calls CheatIO::sendRecv (main.cpp:80-83) and sendCmd publishes all ten MotorCmd topics with mode forced to 0x0A (CheatIO.cpp:44-58), so an MHS publication is overwritten by the controller's next message; the bound topics have a competing publisher

the xacro's velocity_max values are the URDF velocity limits that the joint controller clamps dq to in rad/s (21, and 14 for the calves; joint_controller.cpp:149-150, 216-220); the author's plus or minus 21 deg/s bound was a unit error, and velocity and torque are now operator_required because the clone shows no negative bound

biped.launch starts Gazebo paused by default (biped.launch:7-19) and the README has the operator press start, so the stopped state is also the start state; while physics is paused /gazebo/model_states is silent (and, on simulated time, the 1 kHz controller loop waits), so the explicit model-state read fails NOT_READY after its timeout; the device resource no longer reads it

safe_state.description: The Gazebo world is paused and get_physics_properties read pause true back; the paused flag, not a measured standstill. No unpause is offered: the last MotorCmd stays (joint_controller.cpp:33-45) and this package cannot clear it. The Gazebo GUI or another client can unpause or step the world (a step advances it). Spawn and delete still apply. After mhs.safety.reset the world stays paused; the operator stops hector_ctrl, relaunches biped.launch and presses start outside MHS (Readme.md:61-68).
